topics.topic: Caller outcome when cleanup is unconfirmed and the execution record cannot be persisted
questions: When cleanup is unconfirmed but the store refuses the execution record, what must the caller return, and may it stop without the record despite this passage requiring and asserting that the record was written?

quotes:
An unconfirmed sandbox cleanup is not a refusal: it is
  the separate internal result `stop_required`, returned up the call chain
  after the caller wrote its record; `module:surface` answers
  `internal_error` — here, unlike any other internal error, that record was
  written — and ends the process (State 3, "Unconfirmed cleanup").

If that record cannot be stored,
   the kernel process stops all the same, and recovery executes the element
   again, as it does every function element without a concluded record.
judgement.divergence: One passage requires `stop_required` to follow a successfully written execution record, so recovery finds `cleanup_failed`; the other stops even when the write failed, so recovery finds no conclusion and executes the element again, which the owner and host observe.
judgement.why: The texts assert both that the special stop occurs after and with a written record and that the kernel performs that stop when the record could not be written.

`sandbox` reports that outcome with `SandboxResult.stop_required` true and stops nothing. The module that called
  `sandbox.execute_function` writes the execution's record in its usual store
  call — `runs` the NodeExecution, `functions` the TrialExecution — then does
  nothing more in that request: no further element, no further case, no
  verdict, no activation, no run status. It returns the stop to its caller, and
  `surface` ends the process: during a request after answering it as an
  internal error (A16 rule 7), during the start by stopping the start.

topics.topic: Startup recovery behavior when cleanup of the previous sandbox remains unconfirmed
questions: Before re-executing, what must start-up recovery do about the previous environment whose processes and exchange directory were not confirmed removed, and what happens if their removal still cannot be confirmed?

quotes:
An execution completes only after every process of the environment is reaped
   and the exchange directory is removed. If that cannot be confirmed the output
   is discarded, the execution is recorded `crashed` with detail
   `cleanup_failed`, and the kernel process stops; runs it left `running` are
   recovered on the next start (A14 rule 5). If that record cannot be stored,
   the kernel process stops all the same, and recovery executes the element
   again, as it does every function element without a concluded record.

Every function execution, in trial and in a run alike, runs in a fresh
   isolated environment created by the sandbox: Linux `bubblewrap` with new user,
   PID, IPC, UTS and network namespaces, no network interface but the namespace's own loopback — up, as bubblewrap leaves it in a new network namespace, and reaching nothing outside the execution, so K-02's "no network" holds; this is a property of how the kernel starts bubblewrap, which the kernel does not inspect or verify at run time — the start check (rule 8) asks only that a probe execution succeeds — an environment
   holding only `PYTHONHASHSEED=0` (rule 2), a read-only runtime, and one private exchange directory in which every file the code writes is
   bounded by `sandbox_scratch_bytes_max` (rule 5). No host directory is mounted except the read-only
   runtime and that exchange directory. There is no in-process or fast path.

When the store refused it, the next start executes the element
  again (K-09, A03 rule 7), and the kernel stops on each start for as long as
  the store refuses its records.
judgement.divergence: Recovery may immediately create a fresh execution while a process or directory from the unconfirmed environment remains, or it may first attempt to remove that residue and decline to execute if removal still cannot be confirmed; the host operator observes different processes, disk use, and whether execution starts.
judgement.why: The texts require re-execution in a fresh environment but do not say whether recovery must locate and remove residue from the prior unconfirmed environment or what to do if that residue persists.

events: Startup recovery derives the run as `running` and reaches the recordless function element.
Recovery encounters the surviving process or exchange directory from the previous execution.
outcomes: Recovery launches the required fresh execution while the old process or directory remains.
Recovery attempts removal first and stops without launching the fresh execution when removal still cannot be confirmed.
witness.observer: The host operator observing surviving processes, disk consumption, and whether the recovery execution starts.
